title: The Rust Programming Language
author: Steve Klabnik, Carol Nichols, Chris Krycho, and contributions from the Rust Community
notes: Official living documentation detailing Rust language semantics, ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, and safety guarantees. Published in print by No Starch Press.

title: The Rust Reference
author: The Rust Project Developers
notes: Primary language reference specifying memory layout, drop semantics, and type rules.

title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
author: Randal E. Bryant and David R. O'Hallaron
notes: Core systems architecture textbook covering virtual memory, process address spaces, stack frames, heap allocation, and hardware interaction.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
author: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
notes: Foundational operating systems textbook (Version 1.10) covering virtualization of processor time and physical memory.

title: Modern Operating Systems (4th Edition)
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum and Herbert Bos
notes: Comprehensive systems treatise analyzing kernel architectures, preemptive scheduling, CPU registers, and hardware virtualization.

title: Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface (6th Edition)
author: David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy
notes: Standard university textbook explaining processor execution pipelines, logic gates, arithmetic units, and transistor-level silicon circuits.

title: Milestones: Invention of the First Transistor at Bell Telephone Laboratories, 1947
publisher: IEEE / Engineering and Technology History Wiki
notes: Historical milestone record commemorating the 1947 achievement of the point-contact transistor at Bell Labs.

title: Semiconductor Devices: Physics and Technology (3rd Edition)
author: S. M. Sze and M. K. Lee
notes: Classical physics and engineering text covering solid-state carrier transport, MOSFET gate switching, and microelectronic integration.

title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools (2nd Edition)
author: Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, and Jeffrey D. Ullman
notes: Foundational computer science textbook on lexical analysis, syntax parsing, syntax-directed translation, type checking, intermediate code generation, and machine-code optimization.

title: Engineering a Compiler (2nd Edition)
author: Keith D. Cooper and Linda Torczon
notes: Modern compiler engineering textbook detailing register allocation (graph coloring), instruction scheduling, static single assignment (SSA) form, and intermediate representation architectures.

title: Types and Programming Languages
author: Benjamin C. Pierce
notes: Seminal graduate textbook on operational semantics, lambda calculus, type systems, subtyping, polymorphic typing (System F), and type safety theorems (progress and preservation).

title: Intel® 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manuals
author: Intel Technical Publications
notes: Comprehensive official hardware reference defining instruction encoding, machine opcodes, processor execution modes, memory segmentation, paging, privilege rings, and hardware interrupts.

title: The RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume I: Unprivileged Architecture
author: Andrew Waterman and Krste Asanović (Editors)
notes: Open standard defining an open, modular instruction set architecture (ISA) based on established reduced instruction set computer (RISC) principles.

title: Virtual Memory
author: Peter J. Denning
notes: Seminal ACM Computing Surveys monograph articulating the architectural and theoretical foundations of virtual memory, page replacement algorithms, and the working set model.

title: Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
author: Leslie Lamport
notes: Foundational distributed computing paper introducing partial ordering, logical timestamps (Lamport clocks), and distributed mutual exclusion.

title: The Art of Multiprocessor Programming (Revised 1st Edition)
author: Maurice Herlihy and Nir Shavit
notes: Standard text on shared-memory concurrency, linearizability, mutual exclusion algorithms, lock-free and wait-free synchronization primitives, and memory consistency models.

title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach (8th Edition)
author: James F. Kurose and Keith W. Ross
notes: Authoritative networking textbook examining the protocol stack from the application layer down to the physical layer, covering packet switching, TCP/IP, and congestion control.

title: Computer Networks (5th Edition)
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum and David J. Wetherall
notes: Comprehensive treatise on network architectures, routing algorithms, media access control, error detection and correction, and transport protocols.

title: Distributed Systems: Principles and Paradigms (3rd Edition)
publisher: CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform / Maarten van Steen
author: Maarten van Steen and Andrew S. Tanenbaum
notes: Authoritative guide to distributed architecture paradigms, naming, synchronization, fault tolerance, replication, and distributed consensus algorithms (Paxos, Raft).

title: Introduction to Modern Cryptography (3rd Edition)
author: Jonathan Katz and Yehuda Lindell
notes: Rigorous mathematical treatment of modern cryptography based on formal definitions of security, reductionist proofs, symmetric ciphers, hash functions, and public-key cryptography.

title: Federal Information Processing Standards Publication 197: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
notes: Official U.S. Federal standard establishing the Rijndael algorithm as the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with key lengths of 128, 192, and 256 bits for electronic data protection.

title: Introduction to Algorithms (4th Edition)
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, and Clifford Stein
notes: The standard university algorithms textbook covering asymptotic analysis, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph search, and amortized data structure complexity.

title: The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 1: Fundamental Algorithms (3rd Edition)
author: Donald E. Knuth
notes: Foundational classic of computer science formalizing algorithm analysis, discrete mathematical prerequisites, and essential linear/tree data structures.

title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
publisher: American Institute of Electrical Engineers (AIEE / IEEE)
author: Claude E. Shannon
notes: Landmark master's thesis demonstrating that Boolean algebra could model and optimize electromechanical relay and switching circuits, establishing the theoretical basis for digital logic design.

title: Solid State Electronic Devices (7th Edition)
author: Ben G. Streetman and Sanjay K. Banerjee
notes: Authoritative engineering textbook covering crystal lattices, quantum mechanical band theory, carrier concentrations, p-n junctions, and field-effect transistors.

title: The Garbage Collection Handbook: The Art of Automatic Memory Management (2nd Edition)
author: Richard Jones, Antony Hosking, and Eliot Moss
notes: Comprehensive treatise on automated memory management covering mark-sweep, copying, generational, reference counting, concurrent, and real-time garbage collection algorithms.

title: Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style? A Functional Style and Its Algebra of Programs
author: John Backus
notes: Seminal 1977 ACM Turing Award lecture criticizing the 'von Neumann bottleneck' of mutable state manipulation and presenting functional programming with algebraic program reasoning.

title: The Open Group Base Specifications Issue 7 / IEEE Std 1003.1-2017
author: The Austin Common Standards Revision Group
notes: Official standard defining the portable operating system interface (POSIX) including system interfaces, asynchronous I/O, signals, and process management.

title: Computer Graphics: Principles and Practice (3rd Edition)
author: John F. Hughes, Andries van Dam, Morgan McGuire, David F. Sklar, James D. Foley, Steven K. Feiner, and Kurt Akeley
notes: Classic comprehensive reference on computer graphics fundamentals, affine transformations, rasterization, lighting models, ray tracing, and programmable GPU shaders.

title: Fundamentals of Computer Graphics (5th Edition)
author: Steve Marschner and Peter Shirley
notes: Core graphics curriculum textbook analyzing mathematical foundations, linear transformations, perspective projection, surface reflection, and modern rendering pipelines.

title: The Open Source Definition
author: Open Source Initiative
notes: Standard criteria defining open source software, including free redistribution, source code access, derived works allowance, and non-discrimination.

title: The Cathedral and the Bazaar: Musings on Linux and Open Source by an Accidental Revolutionary
author: Eric S. Raymond
notes: Seminal analysis contrasting centralized, top-down software engineering ('the Cathedral') with decentralized, peer-reviewed open collaboration ('the Bazaar').

title: Database System Concepts (7th Edition)
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, and S. Sudarshan
notes: Authoritative database textbook covering relational models, relational algebra, SQL, indexing structures (B+ trees), transaction management, and ACID guarantees.

title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks
author: E. F. Codd
notes: Foundational ACM paper proposing the relational database model based on mathematical n-ary relations, liberating database users from hardware-dependent navigational pointers.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (4th Edition)
author: Stuart J. Russell and Peter Norvig
notes: The standard worldwide textbook on artificial intelligence, defining intelligent agents, search algorithms, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, and natural language processing.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville
notes: Authoritative textbook covering mathematical prerequisites (linear algebra, probability, information theory), multilayer perceptrons, convolutional networks, sequence modeling, and deep generative models.

title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
author: David E. Rumelhart, Geoffrey E. Hinton, and Ronald J. Williams
notes: Landmark Nature paper demonstrating that backward error propagation through internal hidden representations enables artificial neural networks to learn nonlinear mappings.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd Edition)
author: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto
notes: Foundational treatise on reinforcement learning formalizing Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, temporal-difference learning, Q-learning, and policy gradient methods.

title: Introduction to Linear Algebra (5th Edition)
author: Gilbert Strang
notes: Standard MIT linear algebra textbook explaining vector spaces, linear transformations, matrix factorizations (LU, QR, SVD), eigenvalues, and positive definite matrices.

title: Introduction to Probability (2nd Edition)
author: Dimitri P. Bertsekas and John N. Tsitsiklis
notes: MIT curriculum textbook introducing measure-theoretic probability intuitions, conditional probability, random variables, probability density functions, and limit theorems.

title: Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd Edition)
author: Andrew Gelman, John B. Carlin, Hal S. Stern, David B. Dunson, Aki Vehtari, and Donald B. Rubin
notes: Authoritative reference text on Bayesian statistical inference, prior specification, posterior computation, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), and model checking.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
author: Claude E. Shannon
notes: Foundational paper that established modern information theory, defining information entropy, the bit as a unit of measurement, source coding theorem, and channel capacity limits.

title: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
publisher: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
author: Alan M. Turing
notes: Seminal paper introducing abstract universal computing machines (Turing machines), proving the undecidability of the halting problem, and resolving Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem.

title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation (3rd Edition)
author: Michael Sipser
notes: Authoritative textbook on automata, formal languages, Turing reducibility, computability, and computational complexity classes (P, NP, NP-completeness, space complexity).

title: Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach
author: Sanjeev Arora and Boaz Barak
notes: Comprehensive graduate treatise on computational complexity, circuit complexity, randomized computation, interactive proofs, and quantum computation.

title: An Investigation of the Laws of Thought on Which Are Founded the Mathematical Theories of Logic and Probabilities
author: George Boole
notes: Historical classic establishing algebraic logic, formulating the laws of thought as symbolic operations that represent propositions and truth values algebraically.

title: Convex Optimization
author: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe
notes: Authoritative optimization textbook detailing convex sets, convex functions, duality theory, unconstrained and constrained optimization, interior-point methods, and engineering applications.

title: Speech and Language Processing (3rd Edition Draft)
author: Daniel Jurafsky and James H. Martin
notes: Primary reference on computational linguistics and natural language processing, covering n-grams, word embeddings, transformer architectures, sequence labeling, and syntactic parsing.

title: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications (2nd Edition)
author: Richard Szeliski
notes: Comprehensive survey of computer vision techniques, covering image processing, feature detection, structure from motion, optical flow, deep learning vision models, and 3D reconstruction.

title: The Nature of Statistical Learning Theory (2nd Edition)
author: Vladimir N. Vapnik
notes: Seminal theoretical text establishing statistical learning theory, empirical risk minimization, VC dimension, generalization bounds, and support vector machines.

title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics (3rd Edition)
author: David J. Griffiths and Darrell F. Schroeter
notes: Standard university undergraduate quantum mechanics textbook covering wave functions, the Schrödinger equation, Hilbert spaces, quantum spin, perturbation theory, and Bell's theorem.

title: Über einen die Erzeugung und Verwandlung des Lichtes betreffenden heuristischen Gesichtspunkt
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Seminal paper demonstrating that light is emitted and absorbed in localized energy quanta (later named photons), explaining the photoelectric effect and earning Einstein the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

title: Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Historical paper introducing special relativity, uniting mechanics and electromagnetism by postulating the principle of relativity and the constancy of the speed of light in vacuum.

title: Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Foundational treatise on general relativity establishing that gravity is not a Newtonian force but geometric curvature of four-dimensional spacetime induced by mass-energy distribution.

title: Classical Electrodynamics (3rd Edition)
author: John David Jackson
notes: The definitive graduate textbook on Maxwell's equations, electrostatic boundary-value problems, magnetostatics, electromagnetic radiation, and relativistic electrodynamics.

title: Thermodynamics and an Introduction to Thermostatistics (2nd Edition)
author: Herbert B. Callen
notes: Classic textbook formalizing thermodynamics through axiomatic postulates, Legendre transforms, thermodynamic potentials, and microstate statistical ensembles.

title: Solid State Physics
author: Neil W. Ashcroft and N. David Mermin
notes: Definitive solid-state physics text covering Drude theory, crystal lattices, reciprocal lattice, Bloch's theorem, energy band structures, and electron dynamics in crystals.

title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics (2nd Edition)
author: Bradley W. Carroll and Dale A. Ostlie
notes: Comprehensive astrophysics curriculum text covering stellar structure, hydrostatic equilibrium, nucleosynthesis, degenerate remnants (white dwarfs, neutron stars), and black hole physics.

title: First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole
author: The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration
notes: Historical astronomical achievement presenting the first direct horizon-scale image of the supermassive black hole at the center of the giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87.

title: WMAP Overview & Cosmic Microwave Background
author: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
notes: Authoritative mission archives establishing high-precision parameters for the Standard Model of Cosmology (Lambda-CDM), confirming the universe's age at 13.77 billion years.

title: Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students (4th Edition)
author: Howard D. Curtis
notes: Core aerospace engineering text detailing Kepler's laws, the two-body problem, orbital maneuvering (Hohmann transfers), rocket propulsion kinematics, and satellite perturbations.

title: On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen paradox
author: John S. Bell
notes: Foundational physics paper deriving Bell's inequality, demonstrating that local hidden-variable theories cannot reproduce all predictions of quantum mechanics.

title: Waves and Quanta
author: Louis de Broglie
notes: Historical communication postulating that matter exhibits wave-like characteristics with wavelength inversely proportional to momentum, establishing wave-particle duality.

title: Review of Particle Physics: The Standard Model of Particle Physics
publisher: Particle Data Group / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
author: Particle Data Group
notes: The globally recognized international reference compiling empirical measurements and theoretical consensus on quarks, leptons, gauge bosons, and fundamental particle interactions.

title: Molecular Biology of the Cell (7th Edition)
publisher: W. W. Norton & Company / Garland Science
author: Bruce Alberts, Rebecca Heald, Alexander Johnson, David Morgan, Martin Raff, Keith Roberts, and Peter Walter
notes: The primary worldwide reference text on cell biology, molecular genetics, membrane structure, organelle biochemistry, protein synthesis, and cellular signaling cascades.

title: Principles of Neural Science (6th Edition)
author: Eric R. Kandel, John D. Koester, Sarah H. Mack, and Steven A. Siegelbaum
notes: The authoritative clinical and academic treatise on neuroscience, detailing nerve cells, ion channel biophysics, synaptic transmission, sensory perception, and neural mechanisms of learning and memory.

title: Neuroscience (6th Edition)
author: Dale Purves, George J. Augustine, David Fitzpatrick, William C. Hall, Anthony-Samuel LaMantia, and Leonard E. White
notes: Comprehensive university curriculum textbook on neuroanatomy, neural signaling, sensory processing systems, motor control pathways, and cognitive brain functions.

title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
author: J. D. Watson and F. H. C. Crick
notes: Seminal Nature paper proposing the double-helix molecular model of DNA with complementary base pairing, immediately suggesting a copying mechanism for genetic material.

title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
author: A. L. Hodgkin and A. F. Huxley
notes: Classic electrophysiology paper establishing the mathematical model of voltage-gated sodium and potassium conductances responsible for the generation and propagation of action potentials in nerve axons.

title: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life
author: Charles Darwin
notes: Foundational text of evolutionary biology presenting empirical evidence that biological diversity arises through descent with modification governed by natural selection.

title: Evolution (4th Edition)
author: Douglas J. Futuyma and Mark Kirkpatrick
notes: Standard university evolution textbook explaining population genetics, speciation, molecular phylogenetics, adaptation, and the modern evolutionary synthesis.

title: Loss of recent memory after bilateral hippocampal lesions
publisher: Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery, and Psychiatry
author: William Beecher Scoville and Brenda Milner
notes: Landmark neurosurgical case report on patient H.M. demonstrating that bilateral hippocampal excision produces severe anterograde amnesia, proving that memory consolidation is anatomically localized.

title: A framework for consciousness
author: Francis Crick and Christof Koch
notes: Influential theoretical framework in cognitive neuroscience proposing neurobiological approaches for identifying neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) within corticothalamic circuits.

title: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology (14th Edition)
author: John E. Hall and Michael E. Hall
notes: Comprehensive medical physiology treatise explaining homeostasis, negative feedback regulation, cardiovascular transport, renal clearance, and autonomic nervous system coordination.

title: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine: Discoveries of Molecular Mechanisms Controlling the Circadian Rhythm
publisher: The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet
author: Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine
notes: Official scientific background detailing the discovery of transcriptional autoregulatory feedback loops (PER, TIM, CLOCK) that generate cell-autonomous 24-hour biological oscillations.

title: Epistemology
author: Matthias Steup and Ram Neta
notes: Peer-reviewed philosophical treatise on the nature, sources, and scope of knowledge, truth conditions, justification theories (foundationalism vs coherentism), and the Gettier problem.

title: Classical Logic
author: Stewart Shapiro and Teresa Kouri Kissel
notes: Authoritative reference analyzing propositional and first-order predicate logic, model-theoretic semantics, deductive validity, soundness, and completeness theorems.

title: Scientific Method
author: Hanne Andersen and Brian Hepburn
notes: Historical and conceptual evaluation of scientific methodology, inductivism, hypothetico-deductivism, Bayesian confirmation theory, and historical challenges to universal method.

title: Free Will
author: Timothy O'Connor and Christopher Franklin
notes: Comprehensive survey of metaphysical positions on free agency, causal determinism, incompatibilism, compatibilism, and moral responsibility.

title: Rationalism vs. Empiricism
author: Peter Markie and M. Folescu
notes: Rigorous comparison contrasting the empiricist thesis (all knowledge derives from sense experience) with the rationalist thesis (substantial knowledge is grasped a priori by reason).

title: Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases
author: Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman
notes: Landmark Science paper establishing the heuristics and biases research program, demonstrating that human probabilistic judgment relies on representativeness, availability, and anchoring shortcuts.

title: Working memory: theories, models, and controversies
author: Alan Baddeley
notes: Authoritative review synthesizing the multi-component working memory model: phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, central executive, and episodic buffer.

title: Cognitive load during problem solving: Effects on learning
author: John Sweller
notes: Foundational cognitive science paper introducing Cognitive Load Theory, establishing how working memory capacity limitations constrain schema acquisition during complex problem solving.

title: The Logic of Scientific Discovery
author: Karl Popper
notes: Classical philosophy of science treatise rejecting inductivism and proposing empirical falsifiability as the criterion of demarcation between empirical science and pseudo-science.

title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (4th Edition)
author: Thomas S. Kuhn
notes: Seminal work demonstrating that scientific advancement does not proceed linearly but through periods of normal science governed by paradigms interrupted by revolutionary paradigm shifts.

title: The attention system of the human brain
author: Michael I. Posner and Steven E. Petersen
notes: Landmark neurocognitive paper establishing the three anatomical attention networks: alerting, orienting, and executive control.

title: A Behavioral Model of Rational Choice
author: Herbert A. Simon
notes: Pioneering paper introducing bounded rationality, arguing that human decision-makers satisfice rather than optimize due to cognitive processing and information limits.

title: The Gutenberg Bible at the Library of Congress
author: Library of Congress Rare Book and Special Collections Division
notes: Historical exhibition and provenance records documenting Johannes Gutenberg's perfection of movable metal type printing in Mainz around 1455, marking the dawn of mass print communication.

title: Milestones: First Semiconductor Integrated Circuit (IC), 1958
publisher: IEEE / Engineering and Technology History Wiki
notes: Official IEEE milestone record commemorating Jack Kilby's 1958 invention of the monolithic integrated circuit at Texas Instruments and Robert Noyce's subsequent planar silicon IC at Fairchild.

title: Milestones: Inception of the ARPANET, 1969
publisher: IEEE / Engineering and Technology History Wiki
notes: Official IEEE milestone honoring the transmission of the first message over the ARPANET on October 29, 1969 between UCLA and SRI, pioneering packet switching networks.

title: A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication
author: Vinton G. Cerf and Robert E. Kahn
notes: Seminal paper presenting the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) architecture, enabling decentralized inter-networking across heterogeneous packet-switched communication networks.

title: Information Management: A Proposal
author: Tim Berners-Lee
notes: The original proposal written at CERN formulating a universal linked hypertext information system based on uniform resource identifiers (URIs), HTTP, and HTML.

title: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC
publisher: IEEE Annals of the History of Computing
author: John von Neumann
notes: Historical document (originally issued June 30, 1945) formalizing the stored-program computer architecture: central arithmetic unit, central control unit, memory, and input/output organs.

title: Lighting a Revolution: Electricity and Innovation
publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
author: Smithsonian Curatorial Staff
notes: Curatorial exhibition history detailing the development of incandescent electric lighting, dynamos, and the alternating-current electrical grid engineered by Edison, Tesla, and Westinghouse.

title: Apollo Missions and Lunar Exploration
publisher: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
author: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum Curatorial Team
notes: Authoritative historical treatise chronicling the Cold War technological trajectory of the Apollo program, Saturn V launch architecture, and the 1969 Apollo 11 lunar landing.

title: The Samuel F. B. Morse Papers and the Invention of the Telegraph
author: Library of Congress Manuscript Division
notes: Archival documentation detailing the invention of the electromagnetic recording telegraph and Morse code in the 1830s-1840s, inaugurating the electronic telecommunications era.
